# Supply and demand

## Demand

The law of demand states that, when other things stay the same, a higher price reduces the quantity demanded. A demand curve slopes downward because buyers purchase less as the price rises. A change in income, tastes or the price of related goods shifts the whole demand curve, but a change in the good's own price does not.

## Supply and equilibrium

The law of supply states that, when other things stay the same, a higher price increases the quantity supplied. Market equilibrium is the price at which the quantity demanded equals the quantity supplied. If the price is above equilibrium there is a surplus, and sellers tend to lower their prices. If the price is below equilibrium there is a shortage, and prices tend to rise. In the example in class, the equilibrium price was 8 dollars and the equilibrium quantity was 120 units.
